account:
Today I have been following my appointments and trying to distinguish actual town business from rumours. At the mill I saw 128 hay bales in the stall, priced at two emeralds each, but I did not establish storage arrangements, grain orders, delivery commitments, or a delivery contact. Townsfolk have repeated vague reports of a bridge or port change associated with the bakery. I have not witnessed such a change, and the neighbour could not verify one either.

At tea the neighbour said Freight explicitly has no confirmed safety complaint. He wants confirmed inspection findings and any real freight orders, particularly grain deliveries and contacts. I also heard Freight advertising his ferry and warehouse services. This sounds like an effort to obtain useful information and business, not evidence of a known emergency.

Builder reported that the inn door operates normally and that he fitted an authorized lantern clear of the passage for four emeralds, paid in full. He did not verify sleeping arrangements or certify guest readiness. He also reported no visible defect at the east ferry landing, while stressing that his visit was not a comprehensive structural inspection. Secretary is recording these findings for our office review. No new council correspondence had arrived when I asked earlier.

I have now returned from tea for the sixteen-thirty review, arriving at sixteen thirty-eight. I saw Secretary hand Builder a written book shortly before my arrival. I presume it may be connected with their planned transcription and accuracy check, but I have not read it or heard their explanation yet. The immediate business is to review the written findings carefully, retaining their limitations rather than turning them into unwarranted assurances of safety.
